chunks: From him, from someone else, from Ziyad al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The people will be immoral and not righteous, yet they maintain their kinships, so their wealth increases and their lifespans prolong. So how [will it be] if they were righteous and doing righteous deeds?'
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of maintaining kinship ties on the wealth and lifespan of both righteous and immoral people?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi employs a logical argument from the lesser to the greater (qiyas), noting that even the 'fajarah' (immoral) receive worldly sustenance (wealth and longevity) for maintaining kinship, implying that the 'abrār' (righteous) will receive superior, likely eternal, rewards. It underscores the Shia emphasis on silat al-rahim as a means of divine blessing (barakah) that transcends mere moral status, serving as a practical incentive for social cohesion.

en.hubeali:
From him, from someone else, from Ziyad Al Qandy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The group of the people happens to be immoral and they do not happen to be righteous, so they are maintaining their kinships, and are developing their wealth and prolonging their life-spans. So how would it be if they were righteous, doing righteous deeds?’
en.sarwar: 21. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from more than one person from Ziyad al-Qandy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘A people who are evil doers and not of the virtuous ones but maintain good relations with relatives, their wealth increases, and they live longer. Can one imagine their benefits had they been virtuous and of good deeds?”’
